head: Computer repair
was a boring job.
slides.sub: Geek Squad turned it into something people remembered.

image.label: A black-and-white car parked outside a suburban house at night
image.brief: 1990년대 미국 교외 주택 앞, 밤에 가로등 아래 주차된 흑백 도색의 작은 차. 문짝에 일반적인 배지 모양 마크(실제 로고 아님). 영화 같은 조명.

head: Minneapolis, 1994.
A student with a toolkit.
body: Robert Stephens was a college student in Minneapolis who fixed computers on the side. Home PCs were spreading fast, and so were their problems.
Repair meant hauling a heavy tower to a shop, waiting days and paying a bill no one could predict.

image.label: A cluttered 1990s desk with a beige computer tower
image.brief: 1990년대 미국 가정의 책상. 베이지색 데스크톱 본체와 CRT 모니터, 엉킨 케이블. 젊은 남성의 뒷모습 실루엣, 얼굴 보이지 않게.

slides.label: roughly what Stephens reportedly used to start the business
body: There was no money for a marketing campaign. He was one person competing with repair shops, local technicians and the nephew down the street who knew computers.

image.label: A few dollar bills next to a screwdriver
image.brief: 나무 책상 위에 지폐 몇 장과 드라이버 하나. 소박하고 따뜻한 톤.

head: Tiny budget, many rivals.
How do you get known?
body: You fix computers well. So do plenty of others. Customers can’t tell technicians apart until something goes wrong.

options.text: Buy small ads in the local paper and phone directory
options.feedback: Safe and familiar. But a small ad looks like every other small ad. Keep swiping.

options.text: Make the business itself so distinctive it advertises for you
options.feedback: It costs little, but it risks looking like a gimmick. Keep swiping.

options.text: Undercut rivals with the lowest hourly rate in town
options.feedback: Cheap gets calls, but it also signals cheap work and squeezes margins. Keep swiping.

image.label: A phone directory page full of nearly identical repair ads
image.brief: 1990년대 전화번호부 한 페이지, 비슷비슷한 컴퓨터 수리 광고들이 빽빽하게. 가상의 업체명만 사용.

head: He didn’t hire technicians.
He hired agents.
body: Stephens built a theme. Workers wore white short-sleeved shirts, clip-on ties, black trousers and a badge. Their titles were things like Special Agent.
It looked like a joke. It worked like a promise: neat, serious people arriving to solve a problem.

image.label: A silhouette of a worker in a white shirt, tie and badge
image.brief: 흰 반소매 셔츠, 클립 넥타이, 가슴에 일반적인 배지를 단 인물의 실루엣. 얼굴은 그림자. 1960년대 요원 영화 느낌.

head: The car was
the billboard.
body: Agents drove black-and-white cars with a badge-style logo on the doors. Parked in a driveway for an hour, each car told the whole street who had come to help.
Prices were set per job, not by the hour, so customers knew the cost before work began.

image.label: Neighbors glancing at a black-and-white car in a driveway
image.brief: 교외 주택 진입로에 세워진 흑백 도색 소형차를 이웃들이 지나가며 쳐다보는 장면. 실제 로고·차량 디자인 따라 하지 않음.

head: The costume set
the standard.
body: A uniform raises expectations. If you show up dressed as an agent, you have to be on time, polite and good at the job.
Customers who were nervous about letting a stranger near their computer found it easy to trust, and easy to recommend.

image.label: A worker explaining a repair to a relieved customer at a kitchen table
image.brief: 부엌 식탁에서 유니폼 차림의 수리 기사가 노트북을 가리키며 설명하고, 고객이 안도하는 모습. 인물은 일반적인 모습, 뒷모습 위주.

head: A small local crew.
Then Best Buy called.
body: In 2002, the electronics retailer Best Buy bought Geek Squad, then still a crew of a few dozen people. It kept the name, the uniforms and the cars.
Geek Squad went into stores across the country and grew to thousands of agents.

image.label: A long row of identical black-and-white cars in a parking lot
image.brief: 넓은 주차장에 줄지어 선 같은 디자인의 흑백 소형차들. 2000년대 미국 대형 매장 분위기, 실제 상표 없음.

head: The service itself
became the marketing.
body: Geek Squad made its brand visible at the exact moment customers met it: at the door, in the driveway, at the desk. Every job was an ad.
The theme was not decoration. It made the brand promise visible and pushed staff to keep it.

image.label: A badge, a tie and a car key on a dark surface
image.brief: 어두운 바탕 위에 배지, 클립 넥타이, 자동차 열쇠가 놓인 정물. 실제 로고 없음.

head: Don’t buy attention.
Build it into the work.
body: A distinctive way of delivering your service can do more than ads, as long as the work lives up to it.
**Try it today:** where do customers see you at work? What could make that moment memorable?

image.label: A single black-and-white car driving down an empty street at dawn
image.brief: 새벽빛 속 텅 빈 교외 도로를 달리는 흑백 소형차 한 대.

factChecks.note: 창업 연도(1994), 장소(미니애폴리스), 창업자 Robert Stephens가 미네소타대 학생이던 시절 시작했다는 내용은 Geek Squad·Best Buy 공식 연혁과 주요 언론 인터뷰로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1994년 미네소타대 재학 중 창업 확인.
창업 자본 약 200달러는 Stephens 본인이 여러 인터뷰에서 밝힌 수치로 널리 보도됐습니다. 카드에는 "reportedly"로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 200달러로 창업 확인.
제안된 각도의 '경찰차 스타일 차량'은 정확하지 않을 수 있습니다. Geekmobile은 흑백 도색에 배지 모양 로고를 단 차(초기에는 오래된 Simca, 이후 폭스바겐 비틀 등)로 알려져 있으며, 콘셉트는 경찰보다 1960년대 요원·미션 컨트롤 분위기에 가깝습니다. 카드에는 '흑백 차와 배지'로만 적고 경찰차라고 단정하지 않았습니다.
유니폼(흰 반소매 셔츠, 클립 넥타이, 검은 바지, 배지)과 'Special Agent' 같은 직함은 회사 자료와 보도로 확인하세요.
정액 요금(시간당이 아닌 작업당 고정 가격)은 보도 기준입니다. 구체적 금액은 넣지 않았습니다.
Best Buy 인수(2002)는 사실이지만 인수 금액(보도상 약 300만 달러)과 당시 직원 수(약 50~60명)는 자료마다 달라 카드에는 '수십 명 규모'로만 적었습니다. 이후 매장 확장 규모도 '수천 명'으로만 표현했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2002년 10월 Best Buy 인수, 당시 직원 약 60명 확인.
